observations: Photo 0: Black console with rectangular flat-box shape (resembles Xbox One X form factor, not the tower shape of Xbox Series X/S), Xbox logo visible on front panel, body heavily covered in stickers/decals obscuring vents and surface condition.

Photo 0: TV screen shows an Xbox dashboard with tile layout and 'Connect to the Xbox network' banner, a UI style consistent with the Xbox One generation dashboard rather than the newer Series X/S home screen.

Photo 0/1: Controller is black with a round button above the Xbox button (share button) and textured grips/triggers, a design associated with the Xbox Series generation controller, not the original Xbox One controller.
Photo 1: Screen shows a live football match (FC title) being played, console and controller connected and powered on.
Photo 2: Screen shows 'EA SPORTS FC 26' loading screen, confirming this one game is present and running.
No photo shows the rear of the console (ports, serial/model sticker), the storage/settings menu, the full installed-games list, or any accessories (power brick, HDMI cable, box).

claims.evidence: Photo 0 console shape and dashboard UI style match Xbox One X, not the Xbox Series X tower design; no model text is visible to confirm either way.

claims.claim: 6 games installed: FC26, Far Cry 3, Modern Warfare 3, Dishonored 2, Tomb (Raider, presumed)
claims.evidence: Only FC26 is shown running/loading (photo 1, photo 2); the other 5 titles are not visible on any screen or in a library listing.
Photo 1 shows live gameplay on screen with controller connected, indicating the unit powers on and runs at least one game.

risks.risk: Exact console generation (Xbox One X vs Xbox Series X/S) is unclear and drives price heavily.
risks.proof: Photo of the rear panel showing model/serial sticker, or the console's Settings > System > About screen showing model name.
risks.if_unproven: priced as the lower-value Xbox One X

risks.risk: Body condition hidden under dense sticker coverage (scratches, cracks, melted plastic, missing feet).
risks.proof: Photos of console with stickers removed or at least close-ups of edges/vents not covered.

risks.risk: Controller may be a mismatched/newer-generation controller not originally bundled, or a third-party knockoff.
risks.proof: Close-up of controller back panel showing model number and Xbox certification text.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic/aftermarket controller, not an original matched unit

risks.risk: Only 1 of 6 claimed installed games is visually confirmed; others may not be installed or may be pirated/trial versions.
risks.proof: Screenshot of the full 'My games & apps' library list showing all 6 titles installed.
risks.if_unproven: priced as console with only 1 confirmed game, no added value for the other 5

risks.proof: Screenshot of Settings > System > Storage showing capacity.
risks.if_unproven: priced at base/lowest common storage tier

risks.risk: No accessories (power brick, HDMI cable, original box) shown; buyer may need to source separately.
risks.proof: Photo of all included accessories laid out together.
risks.if_unproven: priced as console-only, no accessories included

proof_requests: Rear panel photo clearly showing the model/serial sticker to confirm Xbox One X vs Series X/S.
Screenshot of Settings > System > About showing model name and storage capacity.
Screenshot of 'My games & apps' showing all 6 claimed games installed.
Close-up of controller's rear label showing its model number.
Photo of the console without stickers or at least unobstructed views of top, sides, and vents.
Photo of included accessories (power cable, HDMI cable, box).
response.reason: The seller's model claim conflicts with what the console shape and dashboard UI suggest, and this console generation is the single biggest price driver, so even a worst-case price cannot be set without a clear model/serial shot.
